key_insight: Fight World Model separates combat rules from video generation: an executable engine decides what happens, while video rendering depicts the results. This aims to make AI-generated combat consistent with game state rather than merely visually plausible.
problem_solved: Existing video world models struggle to maintain persistent combat state and align visible events, such as hit reactions, with rule-based outcomes, such as health changes.
method: Use an executable engine to maintain game state and resolve combat interactions.
Deterministically encode engine-resolved outcomes to guide visual generation.
Separate rule execution from video rendering to support programmable, extensible gameplay.
impact: This architecture offers practitioners a way to pair generative visuals with explicit gameplay logic, potentially improving control and consistency. The supplied abstract is incomplete and does not provide evaluation results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: combat inputs → executable engine → deterministic compiler → video rendering.
Synchronized panels showing a landed hit, its hit reaction, and the corresponding health update.
Comparison sketch: visually plausible combat versus combat constrained by explicit game rules.
State-and-rules dashboard illustrating persistent health values and customizable combat mechanics.
paper_title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
paper_authors: Jiahua Li, Zixu John, Tom Zhong, Fuping Wu, Tianhao Xu
